description: The hieroglyphic symbol representing the number one hundred, used in ancient Egyptian numerology for counting large quantities.
A determinative sign meaning 'among' or 'within', indicating the concept of being inside or surrounded by something.
Depicts an angry facial expression, used as an ideogram to convey wrath or fury in ancient Egyptian texts.
One of the most iconic Egyptian symbols representing life and eternal existence. Frequently held by gods and pharaohs in temple reliefs.
A unit of land measurement equivalent to approximately 2,735 square meters, used in ancient Egyptian agricultural records.
A preposition meaning 'at' or 'near', used to indicate proximity or a specific point in ancient Egyptian grammar.
A determinative representing negative thoughts or evil intentions, often associated with chaos and the god Set.
Represents linen bandages used in mummification rituals. Also associated with medical practices in ancient Egypt.
Symbol of the honeybee, representing the Lower Kingdom. Part of the royal title 'He of the Sedge and Bee'.
A determinative indicating possession or belonging, used to mark words related to ownership and property.
Depicts the act of birth, showing a figure emerging from a body. Used in texts relating to creation and nativity.
Represents the ancient Egyptian board game Senet, symbolizing leisure, strategy, and the journey through the afterlife.
Symbol of knowledge and record-keeping, representing the sacred texts and scrolls used by scribes in ancient Egypt.
Depicts a young male figure, used in texts referring to children, youth, and the concept of infancy.
Represents a tree branch, used in contexts relating to vegetation, agriculture, and the natural world.
Depicts a round loaf of bread, one of the most common offerings to the dead and a staple food in ancient Egypt.
Represents a person brewing beer, reflecting the importance of beer production in ancient Egyptian daily life and temple offerings.
Depicts a person engaged in construction work, associated with the building of temples, pyramids, and monuments.
A determinative meaning 'to bury', used in funerary texts and inscriptions related to burial practices.
Represents an irrigation canal, essential to the agricultural system along the Nile River.
Depicts a piece of cloth suspended from a pole, possibly used as a marker or signal in ancient Egyptian contexts.
The rearing cobra (uraeus), a symbol of divine authority and royal power, worn on the pharaoh's crown.
Represents the advanced composite bow used in ancient Egyptian warfare, symbolizing military strength.
A determinative indicating cooked food, used to classify prepared meals in ancient Egyptian texts.
Depicts a deceased person, used in funerary literature and texts relating to death and the afterlife.
Represents the barren desert landscape beyond the Nile floodplain, associated with chaos and foreign lands.
A determinative meaning 'to divide' or 'separate', used in mathematical and administrative contexts.

Represents the elephant, symbolizing strength and power. Associated with the god associated with chaos in some periods.
A determinative representing an enclosed piece of land or a town, used in place names and geographical texts.
The Eye of Horus (Wadjet), a powerful protective symbol representing healing, restoration, and good health.
Represents woven linen fabric, reflecting the importance of textile production in ancient Egyptian economy.
Depicts a human face, used as a determinative for facial features and expressions in ancient Egyptian writing.
The falcon represents the god Horus and royal power. A central symbol in Egyptian mythology and kingship.
Depicts a finger, used in counting and as a determinative for body parts and gestures.
Represents various species of Nile fish, used in offerings and as a determinative for aquatic life.
The royal flail (nekhekh), a symbol of pharaonic authority paired with the crook in royal regalia.
Represents a neatly folded piece of linen, associated with purity, preparation, and ritual offerings.
Depicts a human foot, used as a determinative for walking, standing, and locomotion-related words.
A mineral used in ancient Egyptian cosmetics and medicine, particularly as kohl for eye decoration.
Represents the giraffe, symbolizing watchfulness and the concept of 'to oversee' due to its height.
A third-person masculine pronoun meaning 'he' or 'him', one of the basic grammatical elements in ancient Egyptian.
Depicts a human head, used as a determinative for head-related words and concepts of thought and leadership.
A third-person feminine pronoun meaning 'her' or 'hers', used in ancient Egyptian grammatical constructions.
A determinative meaning 'to strike' or 'to hit', depicting the act of physical impact.
Represents an animal horn, used as a determinative for horned animals and related concepts.
The title of pharaoh, representing divine kingship and the ruler's role as intermediary between gods and humanity.
Depicts a human leg, used as a determinative for movement, walking, and leg-related actions.
A unit of measurement based on the length of a human arm (approximately 52.5 cm), used in construction.
Represents the concept of vital force or life spirit (ka), one of the essential components of the Egyptian soul.
A determinative meaning 'boundary' or 'limit', used in legal and geographical contexts to define borders.
The lion symbolizes power, ferocity, and courage. Associated with the sun and royal military prowess.
Represents a lizard, used in texts relating to small creatures and as a determinative for reptiles.
Represents a loaf of bread, used as a phonetic complement and as an offering symbol in religious texts.
A specific form of bread offering, frequently depicted on offering tables in tombs and temples.
Depicts a seated man, used as a determinative for male persons, professions, and masculine nouns.
Represents a protective talisman or mascot figure, used in amulets and protective magic.
A determinative meaning 'to meet' or 'to encounter', depicting two figures coming together.
Depicts a mother figure, used in texts relating to motherhood, family, and the divine mother goddess.
Depicts a human mouth, used as a determinative for speech-related words and as a phonetic sign.
Represents a harp or other musical instrument, symbolizing celebration, religious ceremonies, and entertainment.
Represents a species of fish native to the Nile, used in offerings and as a symbol of abundance.
A negation particle meaning 'not', essential to ancient Egyptian grammar for expressing negative statements.
A temporal indicator meaning 'now' or 'at this time', used to mark present actions in hieroglyphic texts.
Represents a nursing figure, associated with childcare and the divine wet nurse in mythology.
Depicts the act of breastfeeding, symbolizing nourishment, life, and the nurturing aspects of goddesses.
A determinative meaning 'to happen' or 'to occur', used in narrative texts to mark events.
The hieroglyphic numeral for one, represented by a single vertical stroke.
Represents the owl, the phonetic value for the letter 'm'. Also associated with the night and wisdom.

Represents a measuring tool or ruler, used in texts related to geometry, architecture, and land surveying.
Depicts a sailing vessel's sail, representing travel, trade, and the navigation of the Nile River.
Represents a sandal or footwear, associated with walking, travel, and the concept of setting forth.
Represents the concept of procreation and creation, associated with the god Khnum and divine creative power.
A smaller ring form used as a determinative for small circular objects and containers.
Depicts a snake (horned viper), used as a phonetic sign and associated with protection and chaos.
Depicts a warrior or soldier, representing military power and the defense of Egypt's borders.
Represents a five-pointed star, symbolizing the sky, celestial bodies, and the divine realm of the gods.
Depicts a walking stick or staff, symbolizing authority, old age, and the journey of life.
Represents the swallow bird, symbolizing rebirth and the arrival of a new season.
A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', used to indicate a specific object or concept near the speaker.
A determinative meaning 'to be dead' or 'death', used in funerary texts and inscriptions about the deceased.
A determinative meaning 'to protect' or 'to guard', associated with divine protection and safekeeping.
A determinative meaning 'to say' or 'to speak', used to introduce quoted speech in hieroglyphic texts.
Represents a turtle, symbolizing patience, longevity, and the primordial waters of creation.
Depicts a horned viper, used as a phonetic sign for the letter 'f' and associated with desert dangers.
Represents a wall or enclosure, used as a determinative for buildings, fortifications, and architectural structures.

Depicts a seated woman, used as a determinative for female persons, professions, and feminine nouns.
A second-person pronoun meaning 'you', used to address the listener directly in ancient Egyptian texts.
